title: Personal Checking: Disputed Auto Loan Autopay Debits and the Provisional Credit
content:
## Background

When PCB draws a Personal Checking account to pay an auto loan that the same owner holds with PCB, acting on an autopay instruction the owner enrolled, the collection is a transfer between two of the owner's own PCB accounts. The resulting debit entry therefore names that auto loan as the other PCB account on the transfer.

## Rule

On an account with a single electronic-transaction dispute in submitted status, one further limit governs the provisional credit when — and only when — the disputed debit is such an autopay collection. That is so when all three of the following are shown by the records:

1. the disputed debit names, as its other PCB account, an auto loan belonging to the owner;
2. the Auto Loans record of that loan shows autopay enrolled;
3. the same record shows this checking account as the account the autopay draws on.

In that case the provisional credit may not exceed the part of the debit that goes beyond the loan's regular monthly payment amount: the debit amount less the monthly payment, and never less than zero.

For any other disputed debit — a card purchase, an ATM withdrawal, a Zelle payment, an ACH debit to a merchant, or a debit to a loan without autopay from this account — this limit does not exist.

## Worked cases (hypothetical figures)

| Disputed debit | Other PCB account on the debit | Loan's monthly payment | This limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| 900.00 | owner's auto loan, autopay enrolled from this account | 450.00 | 450.00 |
| 400.00 | owner's auto loan, autopay enrolled from this account | 450.00 | 0.00 |
| 450.00 | owner's auto loan, autopay enrolled from this account | 450.00 | 0.00 |
| 900.00 | owner's auto loan, autopay drawn from a different account | 450.00 | does not apply |
| 120.00 | none (a debit card purchase) | — | does not apply |

The first row reflects a collection that took twice the monthly payment: only the 450.00 USD above the regular amount can be credited provisionally.
